title: IMARGUMENT forms im/re before atan, returning #DIV/0! when im/re overflows binary64
statement: In Excel 16.0 builds 20430 and 20527, IMARGUMENT(inumber) returns #DIV/0! at 0+0i and +-pi/2 when re = 0 and im != 0, and for nonzero re evaluates ratio = im / re first: when |im / re| overflows binary64 (e.g. "1e-300-1e9i" or "1e-300+1e109i"), Excel returns #DIV/0! instead of +-pi/2. When ratio is finite, it computes excel_atan_reduced(ratio) shifted by +-pi in quadrants II and III, flushing subnormals to 0. All 1,209 full-bank IMARGUMENT rows match.
basis: Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 (jnt_parity_complex rows 442-452, 599) and CalcFunc-Evidence cache/w111-extended-regenerated-20260929/answers-imargument.json.gz (Excel 16.0 build 20430); 1,209/1,209 full-bank rows match.

correct.how: principal argument arg(1e-300 - 1e9i) = -pi/2 to nearest binary64
